refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement says that relative homotopy sets agree for every compact pair and basepoint, but it does not specify the family on Q, require that it be holonomic, or state the smoothness needed to apply the relative theorem. The relative-homotopy definition requires the compared maps to agree on Q; weak homotopy equivalence alone does not provide this relative comparison.

The proof says higher relative statements follow by applying the argument to P×M. A family of immersions M→N supplies injective differential data only in the M directions; it does not give a formal immersion of P×M. The proposed application changes the source dimension and does not establish the family comparison.

The Definition assigns ν_F rank n−m to every formal immersion. The in-scope formal-immersion definition explicitly permits the empty source regardless of dimensions. For M=∅ with declared dimension m=2 and N a point of dimension n=0, the formal pair exists vacuously but the asserted bundle rank is −2, which is not a vector-bundle rank.

The text says open subsets of R^m have no compact component. For m=0, R^0 is a point, and its open subset {point} is a compact component. The example needs a positive-dimension qualification or an explicit no-compact-component restriction.

The Statement asserts that ν_F has rank n−m for every formal immersion. The formal-immersion definition allows M=∅ with m>n, since the fibre condition is vacuous; choosing m=2 and N a point gives a formal pair but would require a normal bundle of rank −2.

The Statement claims that restriction Imm(X×[0,1],N)→Imm(X,N) has contractible fibres. For X a point and N=R, the fibre over 0 consists of immersions of the interval based at 0. Their derivative has constant nonzero sign, so the fibre has increasing and decreasing components and is not contractible.

Proof 1.1 identifies the fibre with the path space of Imm(X,N). For X a point and N=R, Imm(X,N)=R, while an immersion X×[0,1]→R must have nonzero interval derivative; arbitrary paths in R need not, and the immersion fibre has two derivative-sign components. Product immersions carry an extra source-direction derivative, so this path-space identification fails.
The Statement allows n>k≥0 and m≤n but defines the handle as D^k×D^(m−k). It omits k≤m; for k>m the second disk has negative dimension and the handle is undefined.

Proof 1.1 treats the D^(m−k) factor as a parameter in the D^k extension lemma. Slice immersions do not imply an immersion of the full handle: (x,y)↦(x,0) is immersive in the x directions but has differential rank k<m. The cited D^k result supplies no transverse derivatives.

The Statement calls D^k a closed disk, while Given calls it the open unit disk and then requires A⊆D^k to be a closed collar neighbourhood of ∂D^k. The boundary is not contained in the open disk, so these data conflict. The surrounding Statement indicates the likely intended closed disk.

The Statement asserts a parametric deformation relative to the parameter-space boundary without requiring the boundary family to be holonomic. For k=n=1 and N=R, take the constant family on P=[0,1] given by f≡0 and F_x=1. It is formal but not genuine; a homotopy fixed on ∂P cannot end at a genuine family.

Proof 2.1 uses [L2] to obtain collar lifting for data on D^k, but current [L2] states a fibration for immersions of D^k×D^(n−k) restricted to S^(k−1)×[0,1]×D^(n−k). That is a thickened n-dimensional source, not the D^k family in this step; treating the transverse factor as a parameter does not supply its differential data.

The Statement calls Imm_ν and FImm_ν subspaces of the ordinary immersion spaces while saying their data include an identification of the normal bundle with ν_F. Such an identification is extra data. For M a point and N=R, the enriched formal data are R×GL_1(R), with two components, whereas ordinary FImm(point,R)=R; the enriched space is not that subspace.

The sentence “A map with contractible fibres is a weak homotopy equivalence” is false without a fibration or comparable hypothesis. For example, the identity on {0,1} from the discrete topology to the indiscrete topology is continuous with singleton contractible fibres, but changes π0 from two components to one. No fibration property for the stated extension map is established here.

Proof 3.1 uses [L2] to transfer the weak equivalence between the interior and closed disk bundle. The cited collar item claims a contractible-fibre equivalence for Imm(X×[0,1],N)→Imm(X,N), which fails for X a point and N=R because the interval-immersion fibre has two derivative-sign components. That dependency does not license this transfer.

The Statement claims the genuine restriction map is a Serre fibration. Take X=[0,1], A=[0,1/4]∪[3/4,1], N=R, initial lift id, and prescribe g_t(x)=x+2t on the left interval and x−2t on the right. Each g_t is an immersion on A, but at t=1 the left image lies to the right of the right image. A lift path from id must stay increasing, so no extension to an immersion of X exists at t=1.

The proof says a component W of M_0 is a compact clopen subset of M. Compactness and being a component of M_0 make W closed in M, not generally open: in M=R, W=[−1,1] is compact but not open. The conclusion ∂W≠∅ can be repaired by arguing that if ∂W were empty then W would be open and closed.

The Statement permits a continuous family whose restriction to Q is “smooth and holonomic,” while Q is any closed subset of the compact parameter pair. The smoothing supplier and the item’s own Facts [Given] require smooth adjoint data on an open neighbourhood of Q. That neighbourhood hypothesis is missing from the Statement.

[L2] calls the DT-6 proposition “not yet authored,” but the current dependency list includes prop-dual-elimination-of-top-index-handles, which is present in scope and states the required no-top-index-handle result for a nonempty outgoing face. The status/citation text is stale.

The proof calls W a compact clopen subset of connected M merely because W is a component of M_0. A compact component of a compact submanifold with boundary need not be open in M; for example [−1,1]⊂R. Thus the stated reason does not establish that its boundary is nonempty. The conclusion has a short repair: if its boundary were empty, W would be open as well as closed.

The proof says compact images of maps S^k→M imply classes in π_k(Imm(M,N)) or π_k(FImm(M,N)) are represented at a finite source stage M_j. A map into Imm(M,N) is a family of maps defined on all of M; compactness of a map S^k→M gives no finite-stage factorization of that family. The restriction spaces form an inverse-limit problem, and finite-stage equivalences alone do not license the claimed weak equivalence.

The relative clause says a family is “smooth and holonomic over the sub-parameter,” but does not require smooth adjoint data on a neighbourhood of Q. The cited open-source theorem and the smoothing supplier require that neighbourhood condition; the theorem’s own Facts [Given] states it more strongly than the Statement.

Proof 2.1 identifies the enriched fixed-normal-bundle space with the ordinary component containing (f,F). For M a point and N=R, the enriched formal space is R×GL_1(R), with two components, whereas ordinary FImm(point,R)=R is connected. The proof needs a forgetful-fibration/long-exact-sequence comparison; varying bundle isomorphism classes does not make these spaces equal.

reader_findings.evidence: The unrestricted genuine-restriction fibration is false. Take X=[0,1], A=[0,1/4] union [3/4,1], N=R, initial immersion id, and collar homotopy g_t(x)=x+2t on the left and x-2t on the right. Each collar slice has derivative +1; a whole-interval immersion agreeing on both collars must be strictly increasing, which is impossible at t=1. Francis Lectures 5–6, Note 1.4, p.1 gives this obstruction; Lemma 1.3 imposes n>k on the particular thickened-handle restriction. The formal proof also silently needs a continuous boundary-jet extension theorem: a collar and bump do not extend arbitrary smooth jets. Its changing-base pullback is not jointly smooth for merely continuous parameters; compact base does not make the vector-bundle total space compact; local injectivity margins do not supply a uniform finite lifting subdivision; averaging local injections can lose rank. Prescribed terminal lifts are stronger than Serre lifting. A corrected formal-only theorem needs a complete section-extension/fibration proof; genuine lifting needs the actual dimension-qualified Hirsch–Smale argument. Withdrawal/replacement requires Step 5b; item retained.

reader_findings.location: Facts [L1]–[L3]; Proof 1.1–3.1; Given (open versus closed disk)
reader_findings.evidence: The absolute evaluation equivalences are asserted from Francis Lecture 3 Proposition 2.2, whose proof explicitly says it is a sketch; the item supplies neither its parametric contraction nor compatible sections. Pointwise deformation and the defective restriction supplier do not establish a continuous relative deformation. [L2] concerns immersions of the n-dimensional thickening D^k x D^(n-k), rather than the stated k-disk problem, and its genuine fibration is cited without proof. Step 3.1 invokes a relative local h-principle not established by any declared supplier, without constructing the microextension or preserving the prescribed data. Francis Lecture 7 proves only microfibration lifting and defers good position to unavailable Lecture 8. Wilhelm fetch returned 403, so its full argument was not verified. Given also calls the disk open while the Statement uses the closed disk. Needed: a complete absolute family contraction and genuine relative parametric extension proof with exact dimensions and boundary data. Retained for Step 5b rebuild.

Step 1.1 treats D^(m-k) as a parameter in a k-disk immersion theorem. Slice immersion in the k directions does not ensure injectivity of the full m-dimensional differential (the map (x,y)->(x,0) is already a counterexample). No supplier gives compatible transverse derivatives. [L2] is the false unrestricted genuine-restriction assertion. The fibre comparison in 2.1 needs an actual thickened-handle relative h-principle, not the stated core-disk argument; the LES supplies no missing fibre equivalence. The index hypothesis also omits k<=m although D^(m-k) is used. Needed: 0<=k<=m and k<n, a proved genuine thickened-handle fibration, the attaching-collar fibre comparison in all group/component degrees, and its continuous relative family construction. Retained for Step 5b rebuild.

Imm(X x I,N) is not a path space of Imm(X,N): product immersions require an additional independent I derivative. Let X be one point and N=R. Imm(I,R)->Imm(point,R)=R has, over each value at 0, increasing and decreasing components distinguished by the nonzero derivative sign. Its fibre is not contractible and it is not a weak equivalence on pi_0. Formal product data have the same extra derivative datum and two sign components. Path shrinking at s=1 kills the interval derivative. The valid source-dimension-preserving collar theorem needed by the consumers must concern adjoining a collar to a boundary region of a fixed-dimensional manifold, with a separate proof. The present false statement cannot be preserved; proposed withdrawal/replacement remains on disk for Step 5b.

Step 4.1 applies compactness of maps S^k->M to maps S^k->Imm(M,N) or FImm(M,N). Their members are defined on all of M, so they are not represented at a finite source stage. The mapping spaces are restriction inverse limits; finite-stage equivalences alone do not justify equivalence of ordinary limits. Needed: compatible relative extensions fixing prior compact sets, an explicit scheduled homotopy stationary on each compact subset for all sufficiently late stages, and weak jet continuity at the accumulated time, or a proved inverse-limit/fibration comparison. Step 1.1 also requires the product decomposition of mapping spaces over source components and coherent componentwise families; step 2.1 incorrectly calls W clopen in M rather than proving its boundary nonempty. Step 5.1 assumes smooth-near-Q data from smoothness only on Q and cites compact-source genuine smoothing for a noncompact source. False collar and unresolved handle suppliers remain. Retained for Step 5b; no claim that the classical theorem itself is false.

Imm_nu and FImm_nu are called subspaces of the ordinary immersion spaces but also carry an identification of the normal bundle with a fixed nu. Identifications are extra data: for M=point, N=R, the enriched formal/genuine point space is R x GL_1(R), not a subspace equal to ordinary R. Forgetting the identification makes the asserted interval restriction equivalence false, since increasing and decreasing interval immersions give two components over one point component. Francis Lectures 5–6 Definition 1.8 and its pp.3–4 comparison use the enriched spaces and forgetful fibrations. Step 1.1 assumes a tangent splitting of the disk total space without constructing a connection or splitting its vertical tangent sequence. Step 2.1 neither proves contractibility of extension fibres nor a suitable fibration; contractible point fibres alone do not imply weak equivalence. Step 3.1 misuses the false product-collar item to compare interior and closed disk. Needed: properly defined enriched spaces, proved tangent splitting and parametric microextensions, normal-identification forgetful fibrations/LES, and a valid same-dimension collar or germ comparison. Retained for Step 5b.

The proof identifies the space with a chosen normal-bundle identification with an entire ordinary formal-immersion component. Even for M=point,N=R, the identified-normal space is R x GL_1(R), with two components, while ordinary formal point data form R. Varying the fixed bundle isomorphism class does not erase these extra identification fibres or prove the required comparison on families; normal identifications may have monodromy. Francis Lectures 5–6, p.4 uses a square of genuine/formal forgetful Serre fibrations and an LES comparison, which this proof does not supply. The required open-source and thickening suppliers also remain defective. Needed: explicit enriched-to-ordinary fibration comparison covering every source basepoint and target component, with the relative parameter data carried through it. The classical positive-codimension claim is retained for Step 5b proof rebuild.

The Statement extends the comparison to every compact pair and arbitrary compact parameter spaces, while the declared theorem supplies only the specifically defined compact smooth parameter products and relative families with prescribed smooth holonomic data. Weak homotopy equivalence alone does not imply such a comparison for arbitrary compact pairs. The relative target data, their lift on Q, and the smoothness qualifications needed to apply the relative theorem are not specified. Step 2.1 provides no argument for extending beyond that parameter class; applying an immersion theorem to P x M would change the source dimension rather than establish family classification. Needed: an exact formulation with specified relative data and the theorem hypotheses, or a separate mapping-space/ANR or general-compact-pair theorem proving the richer assertion. The ordinary pi_0 deduction is sound conditional on the unresolved main theorem. Retained for Step 5b scope/proof decision.

reader_findings.location: Observed Definition paragraph immediately following the collar data, explaining the two faces
reader_findings.evidence: The originally opened Definition said the incoming and outgoing faces are the two connected components of the boundary decomposition. Each face may be disconnected or empty; the disjoint-union equation alone does not make either a connected component. Batch 1 has since corrected the paragraph to say each face is a union of boundary components and need not be connected. The original mathematical paragraph was read, but its complete original raw carrier was not captured and hashed contemporaneously; no whole-byte historical binding is claimed. Current corrected bytes are not evidence of the old claim. The required correction is already visible and awaits producer/lead reconciliation; no edits to this supplier were made here.
